check_text:
protocol.py: 2 biology problems (2 notes).

1. NOTE NO-NEGATIVE-CONTROL: No no-template control: 7 wells of master mix with a sample
   line 51:  p300_single.dispense(20, well)
   At line 51 the robot starts putting master mix into Bio-Rad 96 Well Plate 200 µL PCR
   (slot 4), and 7 wells end holding it together with a sample. No well on this plate holds
   the mix without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a reagent is
   contaminated, or the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal and nothing
   on the plate can tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6 and A7 in
   slot 4.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6 and A7 in slot 4.
   Fix: Add one well (three for qPCR) with 20 ul of master mix and 5 ul of water in place of
   the template, and tell the plate map where it is.
   Source: MIQE 2009: a no-template control on every plate is essential
           https://gene-quantification.com/miqe-bustin-et-al-clin-chem-2009.pdf
   Source: MIQE 2.0 (2025): the no-template and no-RT controls, still essential
           https://academic.oup.com/clinchem/article/71/6/634/8119148
   Source: Bustin 2025: MIQE compliance remains patchy
           https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12154065/fullTextXML
   Source: Qiagen bench guide: PCR controls (no-template, no-RT, positive)
           https://www.qiagen.com/en-us/knowledge-and-support/knowledge-hub/bench-guide/pcr/reference-genes-and-controls/pcr-controls
   Source: Bio-Rad real-time PCR applications guide: controls in triplicate
           https://www.bio-rad.com/webroot/web/pdf/lsr/literature/Bulletin_5279.pdf
   Source: Thermo Maxima SYBR manual: the NTC contains all components except template DNA
           https://assets.fishersci.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0012933_Maxima_SYBR_Green_qPCR_Master_ROX_Sol__k0251_UG.pdf
   [930a75653857]

2. NOTE UNMIXED-AT-END: 7 wells never mixed after sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4 and
2 more went in (10 to 20% of the well)
   line 58:  p20_single.dispense(5, dest_wells[i])
   At line 58 the robot added sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4 and 2 more to wells A1,
   A2, A3, A4, A5, A6 and A7 in slot 4, which already held master mix and sample 6 (this
   line did it 7 times). The addition was 10 to 20% of the well, nothing mixed the well
   afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do
   not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated.
   A PCR plate is usually vortexed and spun down before cycling; if this one will not be,
   mix it.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6 and A7 in slot 4.
   Fix: Mix wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6 and A7 in slot 4 after line 58: `mix_after=(5, 20
   to 40)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 20 to 40, well)`, with the volume about 80%
   of what the well holds.
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Illumina: normalising library concentrations (pipette up and down 10 times to
   mix)
           https://support.illumina.com/ko-kr/bulletins/2017/03/best-practices-for-manually-normalizing-library-concentrations.html
   Source: Thermo PowerTrack user guide (a reaction plate not mixed well gives variable
   replicates)
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0018825_PowerTrackSYBRGreenMasterMix_UG.pdf
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   [abb1245df84e]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.

findings.title: No no-template control: 7 wells of master mix with a sample
findings.explanation: At line 51 the robot starts putting master mix into Bio-Rad 96 Well Plate 200 µL PCR (slot 4), and 7 wells end holding it together with a sample. No well on this plate holds the mix without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a reagent is contaminated, or the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal and nothing on the plate can tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6 and A7 in slot 4.
findings.fix: Add one well (three for qPCR) with 20 ul of master mix and 5 ul of water in place of the template, and tell the plate map where it is.

findings.title: 7 wells never mixed after sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4 and 2 more went in (10 to 20% of the well)
findings.explanation: At line 58 the robot added sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4 and 2 more to wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6 and A7 in slot 4, which already held master mix and sample 6 (this line did it 7 times). The addition was 10 to 20% of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated. A PCR plate is usually vortexed and spun down before cycling; if this one will not be, mix it.
findings.fix: Mix wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6 and A7 in slot 4 after line 58: `mix_after=(5, 20 to 40)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 20 to 40, well)`, with the volume about 80% of what the well holds.
